findings.evidence: Recounted from inbox-to-memory/scripts/lint-scope.sh:20-21 by splitting each quoted string on whitespace: NOTE_KEY_ORDER = 17 names, so its block is `---` (1) + 17 keys (2-18) + closing `---` on line 19, one line inside the 20-line budget; RECORD_KEY_ORDER = 19 names, closing `---` on line 21; at 18 names (tags/themes mutually exclusive) it closes on exactly line 20. Old text at d4ce6d2 (`git show d4ce6d2:...md | awk 'NR==29'`): "Both key orders below fit inside the budget with room left over, which means overrunning it is almost always accumulated commented-out keys rather than real content." Current machine-contracts.md:29 tail: "The note order's 17 keys close on line 19, one line to spare. The record order lists 19 names and would close on line 21, but `tags` and `themes` are mutually exclusive, so a record carries at most 18 and closes on exactly line 20, with no margin at all. One commented-out key puts a full record over. Adding a name to the record order means dropping one." Grep for "room left over", "almost always accumulated", and "commented-out keys rather than real content" across the file returns nothing. Every number in the replacement (17/19, 19/21, 18/20) matches the recount.

Ruling on the worker's second claim: the row still satisfies C-5 with the precedence fact moved below the table. C-5 requires a "Fails when" description matching behavior; precedence is not a trigger condition but a which-failure-wins fact, and every sibling cell states one trigger. The fact is not lost, it sits two lines under the table at :156 ("`frontmatter-key-domain` is checked ahead of the budget on purpose..."). C-2, not C-5, is the clause that owns precedence, and it is graded against the suite. Observation, recorded and not held against the worker: because "frontmatter-key-domain" now appears twice in the file (:152 and :156), the :565 pin would survive deletion of the table row, whereas the contradiction-fields precedent matches its row uniquely. C-5's check method sets the standard by analogy to that pin and names no mutant, so the identical construct meets it.

findings.description: No assertion was lost. Exactly two require_* lines differ from d4ce6d2, both broken-scope count literals updated in place rather than deleted; every other assertion survives verbatim and all three suites exit 0.
findings.evidence: Extracted every require_*/refute_* line from all three suites at d4ce6d2 and from the working copy, then compared as multisets (counter diff, not just `comm -23`, so a duplicate line can't hide a deletion). inbox-to-memory-smoke.sh: 211 base, 217 current, LOST 2 / GAINED 8. Lost: `require_line "$broken_out" "failures: 18" broken` and `require_line "$broken_out" "v2 files: 19" broken`. Gained includes their in-place successors `failures: 19` and `v2 files: 20`, plus 6 genuinely new assertions. file-issue-smoke.sh and handoff-smoke.sh: 0 lost, 0 gained. Ruling on the worker's first claim, reached independently: the reading holds. C-7 says every call "still runs and still asserts the same thing" — both calls still run, and the thing asserted is the broken scope's arithmetic matching its planted defects, not a frozen integer. C-6 explicitly requires that arithmetic "was updated to match rather than left stale," and C-7's own failing example names the opposite case as the defect ("deleted rather than updated when the new fixture changes the count"). Reading "the same thing" as "the same literal" would make C-6 and C-7 contradict each other and forbid adding any fixture. The literals are correct against the shipped tree: `bash inbox-to-memory/scripts/lint-scope.sh tests/fixtures/inbox-to-memory/broken` prints `v2 files: 20 / total files: 20 / failures: 19`. Nothing else vanished behind them: the multiset diff shows exactly 2 lost lines total across all three suites. Suite runs: tests/inbox-to-memory-smoke.sh exit=0, tests/file-issue-smoke.sh exit=0, tests/handoff-smoke.sh exit=0.
